title: Preview LUT or Baked Look? Check What the Camera Recorded
description: Understand the difference between a preview LUT, recorded Log and a baked look. Check the saved source before making a Rec.709 delivery copy on iPhone.
direct: A preview LUT changes the monitored view; a baked look changes the recorded or exported picture. Seeing normal contrast while filming does not, by itself, tell you which version the camera saved.
figureAlt: Camera monitoring and a saved recording are separate things to check.
figureCaption: AI-generated conceptual illustration, not an App screenshot or measured export.
cards.decision.heading: Start with the distinction
cards.decision.body: A camera app may show a pleasing Rec.709 view while retaining Log footage for later processing. Apple’s Final Cut Camera documentation describes a separate Preview with LUT option. Other camera apps can also offer recording options, so inspect the actual setting and saved clip.
sections.detail-0.heading: Stored pixels and viewing choices differ
sections.detail-0.body: An editor can interpret Log and apply a viewing transform on import. Turning that transform off changes the preview without rewriting the source. A look already rendered into picture pixels cannot generally be removed by toggling a viewer LUT. Retaining the Log original keeps options open; do not judge the file solely by a thumbnail.
sections.detail-1.heading: Make a deliberate delivery copy
sections.detail-1.body: Space Sheep Studio develops VideoFix for iPhone. Its current public listing supports Apple ProRes Log to Rec.709 conversion, with three conversions free before an unlock is required. This guide does not establish support for Apple Log 2, ProRes RAW or arbitrary camera profiles. Conversion makes a new delivery file; it does not reverse a previously baked grade.

steps.step-1.text: Keep the untouched recording and note the camera app, recording profile and whether a look was set to preview only or recorded into the clip.
steps.step-2.text: Open a short saved clip in the intended editor. Check for an automatically applied camera transform before deciding that a flat or contrasty picture is the recorded appearance.
steps.step-3.text: If you have supported Apple ProRes Log footage and need a standard-color sharing file, export a separate Rec.709 SDR H.264 MP4 with VideoFix. Inspect that saved copy in the destination player.
